title: ずいずいずっころばし (Zuizui Zukkorobashi)
description: An Edo-period children's finger-play game song associated with the tea processions (お茶壺道中) that transported precious tea from Kyoto to the Tokugawa shogunate. Villagers were required to stay indoors as the procession passed, a fear reflected in 'おっとさんが呼んでも 行きっこなしよ'. Children play by passing a finger through a fist-tunnel, and whoever is caught when the song ends loses. The lyrics are famously whimsical and nonsensical.
